speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: asked the Acting Minister for Manpower (a) whether the Ministry is taking remedial steps to rectify the instances of erroneous disbursements made by then-SkillsFuture Singapore under the Enhanced Training Support for Small and Medium Enterprises scheme identified in the recent Auditor-General's report; and (b) if so, whether these will have an adverse impact on the businesses or individuals that may have relied on these erroneous disbursements.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
text: asked the Acting Minister for Manpower (a) whether any police report has been filed in relation to the potential gaming by training providers to obtain course fee funding from then-SkillsFuture Singapore as highlighted by the recent Auditor-General's report; (b) whether any efforts will be made to recover any grants that were disbursed to the training providers in question; and (c) if not, why not.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: The Ministry will honour the disbursements which were used to support real training that benefited local workers.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: From my reading of the Auditor-General's report, it said about half the grants, about $2.24 million, were because of erroneous disbursements.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: I understand that the system has been rectified but the disbursements will still go out.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: It said another $2.08 million would have been disbursed under other subsidy schemes.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Does this suggest that there is no issue within the Government that a different subsidy scheme had been used?

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: My first supplementary question is, how will the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) strengthen oversight over the disbursement of the SkillsFuture cost fee funding?

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: For example, will MOM consider taking such steps, such as asking participants to declare whether they are taking courses from a company they or their immediate family members are working for?

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: Also, I could not get the last answer.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: Does the Government have any information on how many SkillsFuture credits were used by course participants on these potentially gamed courses?

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: The investigations on gaming behaviour are still ongoing, so we are unable to reveal more.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: But for all such schemes, including SkillsFuture credits that we give out to support training, there will always be a risk of potential gaming.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: And over time, SWDA will enhance its efforts to detect and investigate different types of gaming behaviours, and where necessary, we will adjust the funding policies to address the risk of gaming.

speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
text: We are also considerate and we want to ensure that individuals have good access to the grants that we give out and therefore, we do not want it to be too onerous on both individual workers and also employers in supporting Singaporeans to access training.
